contract.review_cycle: Per course milestone; in the production analogue, on any change to bureau integration or event taxonomy
contract.steward_role: Credit Risk / Data Engineering, per enterprise_risk_policy.md
contract.disclaimer: Synthetic dataset for a Data Engineering for AI course project. Bureau names, event reasons and score movements are simulation constructs and do not represent real bureau data, real pull practices or FCRA-compliant procedures.

business_definition.summary: One record per credit bureau pull, capturing the bureau queried, why it was pulled, whether it completed, and the score it returned, if any.
business_definition.business_process: Credit bureau inquiry. Pulls occur at initial application and again for refreshes, corrections, fraud verification and manual review. This is the only event-stream dataset in the project and the only one carrying history rather than a single snapshot.
business_definition.role_in_architecture: Event fact table. It is the audit trail behind the point-in-time values that appear as single fields elsewhere: loan_application.fico_score is derived from it, and it is the raw material for reconstructing what was known about an applicant at any given date.
answers_questions: How many times was this applicant pulled, from which bureaus, and why?
What score did the bureau return at each pull, if any?
Which pulls failed, are pending, or were resubmitted?
What was known about an applicant as of a given date?
does_not_answer: The applicant's risk tier. This stream carries no tier field; the policy tier is applicant_risk_features.risk_tier.
A continuous score history. Each pull is a single observation from one bureau, and consecutive pulls may come from different bureaus.
Why a score moved. event_reason describes why the PULL was initiated, not what changed on the credit file.
Anything about applications, products, decisions or eligibility. No such fields exist here.
business_definition.in_scope: 1,775 pulls across 580 of the 600 applications (the 20 NO_HISTORY applications have no pulls), dated 2022-08-16 to 2026-11-29, a window that begins roughly 17 months before the earliest application.
business_definition.out_of_scope: Tradeline detail, inquiry records, dispute outcomes, permissible-purpose documentation, and the content of the credit file beyond the score.

grain.declared_grain: One row per credit bureau pull event.
grain.foreign_key: application_id → loan_application.application_id (580 of 600 applications present; 1 to 5 events each, mean 3.06; the 20 NO_HISTORY applications have none)
grain.fan_out_warning: CRITICAL: this is the only many-side table in the project. Joining it to loan_application.csv multiplies application rows by roughly 3, and an inner join also silently drops the 20 NO_HISTORY applications. Any sum over requested_amount_usd, any application count, and any approval rate computed after a naive join is wrong by that factor. Aggregate to one row per application BEFORE joining, typically the latest pull with a returned score on or before the application date.
grain.grain_is_not_a_state: A row is an observation event, not a state of the applicant. Two events on the same day for the same application are two pulls, not a contradiction. One duplicate application-and-date pair exists in the current snapshot.
grain.event_vs_entity: fico_score describes what THAT pull returned, not a durable applicant attribute. Do not treat it as 'the applicant's score' without an as-of qualifier. The score as of the application date is already materialised as loan_application.fico_score.

event_date.format: ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) — note this differs from loan_application.date, which is M/D/YYYY
event_date.notes: The date the pull occurred. The only temporal anchor in the row; there is no separate ingestion or effective timestamp.

fico_score.notes: What this pull returned. Populated on all 1,741 Completed and Resubmitted pulls; empty on the 34 Error and Pending pulls, which returned no result.

bureau_source.notes: Roughly even split (576 / 600 / 599). 69.5% of applications with pulls (403 of 580) have pulls from more than one bureau.

event_status.notes: Processing outcome of the pull. 5.1% of events are not Completed (57 Resubmitted, 33 Error, 1 Pending).

event_reason.scale: Initial Application, Credit Refresh, Manual Review, Fraud Verification, Re-Pull After Correction
event_reason.notes: Why the pull was initiated. Not a reason for any score movement.

point_in_time_semantics.as_of_meaning: The date the bureau was queried. fico_score describes what was known as of that date and nothing later.
point_in_time_semantics.temporal_nature: Append-only event stream. Events are immutable once written; a correction appears as a new event with reason Re-Pull After Correction rather than an edit to the original.
point_in_time_semantics.pre_application_coverage: The stream begins roughly 17 months before the earliest application, so pulls predating an application exist for every application with credit history. Each of the 580 applications with pulls has at least one pull with a returned score on or before its application date, and every pull falls inside the 24 month lookback. The 20 NO_HISTORY applications have no pulls at all.

leakage_status.current_state: 0 of 1,775 events post-date their own application's date, and check_source_consistency.py asserts it. A join written without a date filter currently returns correct results. 18 pulls are dated after the 2026-09-14 extract date; all belong to future-dated applications, which ingestion quarantines.
leakage_status.why_the_control_still_applies: That correctness is a property of how this snapshot was generated, not a constraint the data enforces. The event taxonomy explicitly includes post-decision reasons such as Credit Refresh and Re-Pull After Correction, so post-application events are expected in any realistic extension. An unfiltered join is currently untested rather than safe, and would begin leaking silently the moment such an event appears.
leakage_status.required_practice: Write event_date <= as-of date as a join predicate regardless, and assert the violation count at load so the number of post-application events is observed rather than assumed.

point_in_time_semantics.reconstruction_pattern: To recover what was known at an application date: filter to event_date <= application date AND fico_score not empty, sort by event_date, take the last row per application, and read fico_score. This reproduces loan_application.fico_score on 580 of 580 scored applications. Filtering on event_status = 'Completed' instead is wrong: it drops Resubmitted pulls, which carry a returned score and supply the application score for 19 applications. Omitting the date filter admits the future.
point_in_time_semantics.chain_discontinuity_warning: Each row is one observation from one bureau on one date. The prior_fico, prior_tier, new_tier and tier_changed_flag columns were dropped in the 2026-10-01 data, so there is no before-and-after pair to chain. Read fico_score at each event date as an independent observation and do not infer what happened between two pulls.

source_of_truth.system_of_record: Credit bureau integration layer (simulated). Authoritative for the history of what was pulled, from whom, when, and with what result.
authoritative_for: The existence, date, bureau and reason of every pull
What each bureau returned at each pull (fico_score), including that Error and Pending pulls returned nothing

The FICO on the application record. loan_application.fico_score is derived from this stream as the score of the latest pull with a returned score on or before the application date, and matches it on 580 of 580 scored applications. This stream is the source of truth; the application field is a materialised view of it.

not_authoritative_for.reason: This stream carries no tier field. The policy tier is scored from delinquency, debt burden and overdue amount points, not from the FICO score; the stream feeds it only through credit_history_months_observed, which covers the oldest returned pull inside the 24 month lookback.
This dataset contains no application, product or decision fields at all.

source_of_truth.multi_bureau_caveat: 69.5% of applications with pulls have pulls from more than one bureau. Bureau scores are not interchangeable: a movement between consecutive events may reflect a different bureau rather than a change in the applicant's credit. Always read bureau_source alongside any score comparison, and do not compute a delta across bureaus without saying so.
downstream_consumers: Retrieval / RAG index over the applicant corpus

freshness.delivery_mode: Append-only event stream, delivered as a full-file snapshot
freshness.expected_cadence: Continuous in the production analogue; snapshot-stable per project milestone
freshness.max_acceptable_staleness: 24 hours in the production analogue. A missing recent pull means point-in-time reconstruction silently returns an older observation rather than failing.
freshness.freshness_signal: MAX(event_date) against the current date, plus event count
freshness.staleness_alerting: Alert on: any drop in row count (the stream is append-only, so a decrease means data loss); any application_id not resolving to loan_application.csv; any new value in event_status, event_reason or bureau_source; a score on an Error or Pending pull, or an empty score on a Completed or Resubmitted pull; a material rise in the non-Completed share above the current 5.1%.
freshness.late_arriving_data: Expected. Pending events resolve later and Resubmitted events follow failures, so an applicant's event set is not final at any given extract. Reconstructions run at different times can legitimately differ — record the extract date alongside any derived feature.
freshness.backfill_policy: Append-only. Corrections arrive as new events with reason Re-Pull After Correction, never as edits, so history is preserved by construction.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: Only pulls with a returned score carry a fico_score.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: The 1,684 Completed and 57 Resubmitted pulls carry a score; the 33 Error pulls and 1 Pending pull returned no result and carry an empty fico_score. An empty value means no bureau result, not a zero and not a gap to impute. Filter on fico_score not empty before using any score, and treat a 'latest pull' that can land on an Error or Pending row as a defect.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: This table fans out; aggregate before joining.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: 1,775 events against 580 of the 600 applications. A naive join triples application rows and inflates every sum, count and rate computed afterwards, and an inner join drops the 20 NO_HISTORY applications. Reduce to one row per application first, normally the latest pull with a returned score on or before the application date.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: Events are observations, not a continuous timeline.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: Each pull is one score from one bureau on one date. Do not treat the difference between two pulls as evidence of what happened on the credit file between them, and do not interpolate a score between event dates. Read fico_score at each event date as an independent observation.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: event_reason explains the pull, not the score.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: Fraud Verification, Manual Review, Credit Refresh and Re-Pull After Correction describe why the inquiry was initiated. A model or a summary that attributes a score movement to the reason code — 'the score dropped because of fraud verification' — is inventing causation. Note also that Fraud Verification and Manual Review are operational reasons that may correlate with outcomes; using them as model features risks encoding decision-process artefacts rather than credit risk.

69.5% of applications with pulls have pulls from more than one bureau. A 15-point 'movement' between consecutive events may simply be Equifax versus TransUnion. Any delta must name both bureaus or be restricted to a single bureau.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: Pull frequency is an operational signal, not a credit signal.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: Applications with credit history have 1 to 5 pulls; the 20 NO_HISTORY applications have none. A high count reflects how the file was processed (refreshes, corrections, fraud checks), not the applicant's creditworthiness. Using pull count as a risk feature encodes the institution's own handling of the case, which is close kin to the prohibited-factor problem in applicant_risk_policy.md.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: Absence of post-application events is a property of this snapshot, not a guarantee.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: 0 of 1,775 events post-date their application today, so unfiltered joins happen to work. The event taxonomy anticipates post-decision pulls, so this will not hold in any realistic extension. Keep the date predicate and assert the violation count at load rather than relying on the current shape of the data.

business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.rule: Retrieval must carry the event date, bureau and status.
business_interpretation_consumers_must_p.detail: A chunk reading 'APP100220: FICO 702' is materially incomplete. It must read as an observation: 702, reported by TransUnion, on 2026-03-14, from a completed Manual Review pull. Without those qualifiers the value reads as the applicant's current score and can be mistaken for the score the application was decided on.

field_semantics.event_id: Primary key of the pull event (E#######). Appears nowhere else. Ids do not follow date order and carry no sequence meaning.
field_semantics.application_id: Join key to loan_application.csv and applicant_risk_features.csv. 1 to 5 events per application for 580 applications; the 20 NO_HISTORY applications have none.
field_semantics.event_date: Date the bureau was queried. ISO 8601 here; M/D/YYYY in loan_application.csv.
field_semantics.fico_score: Score returned by this pull. Valid only as an observation at event_date, from bureau_source. Populated on Completed and Resubmitted pulls; empty on Error and Pending pulls.
field_semantics.bureau_source: Equifax, Experian or TransUnion. Required context for any score comparison.
field_semantics.event_status: Completed, Pending, Resubmitted or Error. Completed and Resubmitted pulls carry a returned score; Error and Pending pulls carry none.
field_semantics.event_reason: Why the pull was initiated. Operational metadata, not a cause of score movement.

prohibited_uses: Imputing a score for an Error or Pending event, or treating its empty fico_score as zero.
Presenting fico_score without its event date, bureau and status.
Using pull count, event_reason or event_status as model risk features.
Banding fico_score into T1-T5 and presenting the result as the policy risk tier.
referenced_authorities: Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) — permissible purpose for each inquiry, accuracy of reported information, and the consumer's right to dispute; this project does not capture permissible-purpose documentation, which would be required in a real system
Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) — adverse action notices must cite accurate information from the file actually relied upon
applicant_risk_policy.md (RISK-TIER 1.0) — the 24-month lookback and the prohibition on post-application credit events
gaps_relative_to_a_real_system: No permissible-purpose field, so FCRA compliance of any individual pull cannot be evidenced from this data.
No soft/hard inquiry distinction, which affects both consumer impact and score treatment.
No dispute or reinvestigation outcome linkage for Re-Pull After Correction events.
event_reason is randomly assigned in this synthetic data, so it carries no real operational pattern.
compliance_notes.escalation: loan_application.fico_score is derived from this stream, so any disagreement with the latest returned score on or before the application date is a lineage defect, not a design feature. Resolve it by re-deriving the application field from the stream, never by editing an event. Genuine anomalies (a dropped event count, an unresolvable application_id, a new status value, a score on an Error or Pending pull) are held pending documented resolution per enterprise_risk_policy.md section 3.

change_log.summary: Initial semantic contract. Event grain and fan-out, as-of and reconstruction semantics, chain discontinuity, as-of-scoped source-of-truth boundaries, freshness with late-arriving events, and ten interpretation rules derived from a full profile of 1,835 events across 600 applicants.

Updated for the regenerated data: prior_fico, prior_tier, new_tier and tier_changed_flag removed, new_fico renamed fico_score (empty on Error and Pending pulls), join key corrected to application_id, and counts reprofiled to 1,775 pulls across 580 applications. loan_application.fico_score is now derived from this stream, so the as-of-scoped authority text, chain discontinuity material and BI-C05 and BI-C07 were rewritten or dropped.
